summary: A 1954 L-4 tower on Middle Sister Peak in northern Idaho replaced a 1951 tower that burned in 1953; volunteers have staffed and restored it since the 1990s.

staffing.as_of: undated; Idaho Fire Lookouts staff list runs through 2026

access.note: Listed as drive-up and staffed by Idaho Fire Lookouts. No closure or permit requirement is mentioned in the sources.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (St. Joe Ranger District, cooperator); the forest name differs between sources

corrections.why: 10.7 m is 35 ft, the height of the 1951 tower that burned in 1953. The standing tower is a 30-ft tower, per the register and firelookout.com.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register places the lookout in the Idaho Panhandle National Forest. Firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and Spokane Historical name the St. Joe National Forest. The story reports both names.
The register gives 6,818 ft (2,078 m), which matches the record's elevation_m. Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 6,898 ft. The story reports both figures.
Idaho Fire Lookouts says staffed every summer, firelookout.com says most summers, and the register says volunteers have staffed it since 1992. The story reports the differences.

notes_for_editor: History is consistent across sources; the forest name, the elevation (6,818 vs 6,898 ft) and staffing frequency conflict. The height correction assumes the record's height_m describes the standing 30-ft tower. Spokane Historical is a photo caption and is used only for the 1951/1953 sequence and the North Idaho claim. The Idaho Fire Lookouts 1951 entry prints 35 with a double-prime, so the 35-ft figure is taken from the NHLR and Spokane Historical. Staff names from Idaho Fire Lookouts are omitted on purpose.
